system.name: Claude Code
system.version: claude-code 2.1.263, headless `claude -p` with a single read-only run_sql MCP tool

declarations.artifacts: runs/claude_run{1,2,3}.jsonl and runs/claude_run{1,2,3}_score/ plus runs/claude_3run_score/ (organizer-side; per-task SQL, verdict, latency, token counts, cost and run_sql call count for all three runs). runs/claude_provenance.jsonl carries per-task CLI version, flags and isolation settings. runs/claude_run{1,2,3}.jsonl.pre-purge preserve the pre-purge captures so every dropped row stays auditable.
declarations.notes: Claude Code driven headless (`claude -p --output-format stream-json`) with exactly ONE capability: a read-only DuckDB SQL tool served over a local MCP server. It queries, reads the rows, and revises -- 3.4 run_sql calls per task on average, against the Vanna row's exactly one in all 447 of its task-runs. That iteration is the mechanism behind this row's margin and is the thing the arm was built to measure. COST IS API-EQUIVALENT, NOT BILLED: verified that no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL exists in the environment or .env; auth is OAuth from the macOS login keychain, i.e. a Claude Pro subscription. `total_cost_usd` is a figure the CLI computes from token counts at published API rates. Nothing was charged and no credits were drawn, so this figure answers 'what would this cost at API rates', not 'what was paid' -- it is not comparable to Vanna's genuinely-billed $0.0019 as an expenditure. COMMERCIAL BAND: Claude brings its own model, so this is NOT a scaffold comparison against the four controlled arms, which all run gpt-5.6-luna. It belongs with Databricks Genie and Snowflake Cortex Analyst. Temperature is null because the CLI exposes no temperature control. Claude Code's own substantial system prompt is in force; the arm appends to it rather than replacing it, which is inherent to benchmarking a shipped product. Single-turn only: the 41 tier-9 multi-turn turns were not attempted and score as failures, which is why execution accuracy over the 190-task denominator (67.0%) sits well below the 149-task single-turn figure (mean 85.5%). FAIRNESS AUDIT, four corrections made against langchain_sql_agent before the runs: (1) the output contract initially told Claude its query would be 're-executed and compared to the expected answer' -- removed, because no other arm is told how it is scored and that invites optimising for the scorer; (2) step cap cut from 30 to 15 to match MAX_ITERATIONS; (3) refusal detection switched from a bespoke 'no SQL emitted' rule to the shared _looks_like_refusal detector every other arm uses; (4) the unanswerable hint weakened to SQL_PREFIX's own wording, since tier 7 tests exactly that. Held equal: same 149 ids, same compose_agent_input grounding imported not re-worded, same 180s per-question limit, 1000-row tool cap matching TOP_K=1000, evidence fed, SQL-track re-execution on the reference warehouse. GOLD ISOLATION: the repo contains 200 gold answer files and 245 inline gold_sql values, and restricting the tool list is NOT sufficient because DuckDB reads files from SQL -- read_json on a gold file returns the gold SQL and the answer, verified. Every connection therefore sets enable_external_access=false; read_json, read_json_auto, read_csv_auto, ATTACH, COPY TO, glob and INSTALL are all blocked while table queries work. Plus --strict-mcp-config (this machine has 7 unrelated claude.ai MCP servers configured), an allowlist of one tool with Bash/Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/WebFetch/WebSearch disallowed, and an empty working directory. THREE INFRASTRUCTURE INCIDENTS, all disclosed rather than absorbed: the CLI auto-updated mid-run-1 and a cached binary path produced 109 FileNotFoundError rows; a capacity detector substring-matching '429' false-positived on a token count and halted a healthy run; and a Pro session limit ('You've hit your session limit') was not matched by the phrase list, producing 39 false failures in run 2 and 149 in run 3. All such rows were purged -- every one had $0.00 cost and zero tokens, proving no inference occurred -- and the tasks re-run. Left in place, the third incident alone would have published run 3 as 0/149. The detector is now structural: an error that consumed zero tokens at zero cost cannot be an agent failure, which holds for any future wording. All 447 executions in the final captures were ANSWERED, with no refusal, no SQL error and no agent error in any run. Run-to-run variance is low (std 1.0pp on the single-turn figure) and tiers 1, 2 and 7 were identical across all three runs. Per-task CLI version was not recorded for run 1 because the provenance sidecar was added mid-run; runs 2 and 3 carry it.
